facts.fact: Geotargeting is defined by the page as delivering content to a consumer via mobile or web using the recipient's geographic location information.
facts.quote: Geotargeting is the practice of delivering content to a consumer—via mobile or web—using the geographic location information of the recipient.

facts.fact: StackAdapt says zip/postal code targeting, where advertisers upload a list of codes to reach users, is available within the US and Canada.
facts.quote: Within the US and Canada, you can upload a list of zip codes/postal codes to reach users.

facts.fact: StackAdapt says geo radius targeting in mobile in-app environments can be customized down to the mile or kilometre.
facts.quote: customizing your radius down to the mile/kilometre to target users in mobile in-app environments.

facts.fact: A third-party eMarketer report, as quoted by StackAdapt, says connecting with consumers within 2 to 3 miles of a location is far more effective than real-time in-store geofencing for retail and QSRs.
facts.quote: connecting with somebody within 2 to 3 miles of that location.
